phase: Repository Execution Governance Hardening — Terminal Assessment
purpose: Freeze the current GitHub Actions execution-governance boundary after the post-v0.3.0 hardening series, so future work can distinguish a genuine execution-policy change from repeated re-auditing of an already closed workflow surface. This assessment is repository governance only and has no authority to change scientific model state.

hardening_series.interpretation: The series established an exact write-permission boundary, explicit workflow permissions, audit-script execution coverage, guarded historical live-acquisition CLIs, manual/evidence-triggered live-provider paths, fully offline Scientific CI, executable-command-aware pull-request provider-access regression protection, synchronized Unreleased versioning rationale, and a repository-wide prohibition on pull_request_target.

established_invariants: Every GitHub Actions workflow declares top-level permissions explicitly.
Write permission is confined to the exact allowlist enforced by the central Actions governance audit.
Only contents: write is permitted within the write-capable allowlist.
The privileged pull_request_target event is forbidden repository-wide unless the governance contract is deliberately redesigned.
Ordinary pull_request workflows may not directly execute provider-network-capable scripts or inline curl/wget provider access.
Scientific CI is an offline verification path on ordinary pull_request and push execution.
Every scripts/audit_*.py executable has a workflow execution path and workflow audit references resolve to existing scripts.
Completed or frozen live-source acquisition paths are manual, evidence-triggered, or require explicit live-refetch acknowledgement as applicable.
explicit_non_claims: Execution-governance closure does not prove external-source truth or provider availability.
Execution-governance closure does not complete the Accounting Spine.
Execution-governance closure does not validate behavioural mechanisms or causal interpretation.
Execution-governance closure does not authorize calibration, refit, holdout opening, feedback activation or behavioural closure.
Execution-governance closure does not require or authorize a public version bump.
reopen_conditions: A GitHub Actions workflow is added, removed, or materially changes trigger or permission topology.
A workflow gains or changes write capability or a new write permission scope is required.
A future design requires pull_request_target or another privileged pull-request execution context.
Scientific CI gains a live-provider execution path or ordinary pull-request execution gains direct provider access.
An audit script loses its workflow execution path or a workflow gains a dangling audit-script reference.
A retained live-source path changes from manual/evidence-triggered semantics or removes an explicit live-refetch safeguard.
Scientific CI or an execution-governance regression test demonstrates a broken invariant.
A future release or repository architecture milestone deliberately changes the execution-governance contract.
